english: I think / it seems / it looks like (a softened guess or opinion)
formNote: For verbs in the present, attach -는 것 같아요 to the stem (가다 → 가는 것 같아요). For adjectives, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 (춥다 → 추운 것 같아요, 비싸다 → 비싼 것 같아요). For the past, use -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요 with verbs (먹었다 → 먹은 것 같아요) and for the future/guess use -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요. In speech 것 is almost always shortened to 거: -는 거 같아요.
usage: Soft opinion — sounds more polite than 맛있어요
Guess about the future → -ㄹ 것 같아요
examples: 이 카페 사장님이 좀 바쁘신 거 같아요.
I think the cafe owner is a bit busy.
거 같아요 is the natural spoken form of 것 같아요
저 둘 사귀는 거 같지 않아?
Don't those two seem to be dating?
Casual -는 거 같다 used to gossip with a friend
제가 길을 잘못 든 것 같은데, 여기 어디예요?
I think I took a wrong turn — where is this?
Hedging your own mistake politely
mistakes: Using -는 것 같다 with adjectives: 춥는 것 같아요 is wrong — adjectives take -ㄴ (추운 것 같아요).

english: decided to / made up my mind to (often a plan or promise)
formNote: Attach -기로 하다 directly to any verb stem with no sound change (운동하다 → 운동하기로, 끊다 → 끊기로). The decision is reported in the past tense (했어요) because the deciding already happened. Negative: V-지 않기로 했어요 or V-기로 안 했어요 (the first is more natural).
usage: I decided to cut down on drinking
I decided not to work overtime
examples: 올해는 진짜 돈 좀 모으기로 했어요.
This year I've really decided to save some money.
Spoken resolution; 진짜 adds determination
우리 다음 주에 한강 가서 치맥 하기로 했어.
We decided to do chicken and beer at the Han River next week.
치맥 = fried chicken + beer, a staple young-adult plan
회사랑 얘기해서 재택근무하기로 했어요.
I talked with the company and we decided I'd work from home.
Work context; 재택근무 = WFH
mistakes: Saying -기로 해요 (present) for a decision already made — use the past -기로 했어요.

english: ended up (completely) doing it — finished it off, often with regret or relief
formNote: Take the verb's -아/어 form and add 버리다, then conjugate that (먹다 → 먹어 버리다, 가다 → 가 버리다, 잊다 → 잊어 버리다). Stems with ㅏ/ㅗ take -아 버리다, others take -어 버리다; 하다 → 해 버리다. It adds the nuance of doing something fully/irreversibly — sometimes regret (oops), sometimes relief (good riddance). In fast speech 버렸어요 often becomes -아/어 버렸어 or contracts further.
usage: I ended up eating it all
I just got it all done
Here it's relief — finished it off
examples: 월급 들어오자마자 다 써 버렸어요.
I blew my whole paycheck the moment it came in.
Money regret — very relatable for 20s-30s
고백했는데 차여 버렸어... 술이나 마시자.
I confessed but got rejected... let's just drink.
Casual; 차이다 = get dumped/rejected
귀찮아서 그냥 배달시켜 버렸어요.
I couldn't be bothered so I just ordered delivery.
배달시키다 = order delivery; 버리다 adds the 'just did it' feel
mistakes: Mixing up the vowel: 가 버리다 not 가어 버리다, and 와 버리다 not 오아 버리다.

english: I'm worried that... / in case... (anxiety about something happening)
formNote: Attach -ㄹ까 봐(요) to stems ending in a vowel (가다 → 갈까 봐, 오다 → 올까 봐) and -을까 봐(요) to stems ending in a consonant (늦다 → 늦을까 봐, 밀리다 → 밀릴까 봐). For a worry about the past, use -았/었을까 봐요 (놓쳤을까 봐요 = worried I missed it). Mid-sentence it becomes -(으)ㄹ까 봐(서) + a clause explaining what you do because of the worry.
usage: I brought an umbrella in case it rains
I don't eat it because I'm afraid of gaining weight
I didn't say it for fear of getting scolded
examples: 면접에서 떨릴까 봐 어제 잠도 못 잤어요.
I was so worried I'd be nervous in the interview that I couldn't sleep.
Job-hunting anxiety
답장 안 오길래 차단당했을까 봐 걱정했잖아.
You didn't reply so I was worried I'd been blocked.
Past worry → -았을까 봐; 차단 = block on messenger
월세 밀릴까 봐 알바 하나 더 구했어요.
I got another part-time job in case I fall behind on rent.
월세 = monthly rent, 알바 = part-time job
mistakes: Confusing it with -(으)ㄹ까요? (a suggestion/question). -(으)ㄹ까 봐요 is about WORRY, not asking 'shall we?'

english: (someone) said that... — reporting a statement someone made
formNote: For verbs, attach -ㄴ다고/-는다고 to the stem (가다 → 간다고 했어요, 먹다 → 먹는다고 했어요). For adjectives, attach -다고 directly (춥다 → 춥다고 했어요). Past tense uses -았/었다고 했어요 for both. In casual speech this contracts to -대(요): 간대요 (= 간다고 해요), 바쁘대 (= 바쁘다고 해). For nouns the form is N(이)라고 했어요.
examples: 팀장님이 오늘 회식 있다고 했어요.
The team lead said there's a company dinner today.
회식 = team dinner, common work word
걔가 너 좋아한다고 했어! 진짜야.
He said he likes you! For real.
Casual gossip; 걔 = that person/he
집주인이 보증금 올린다고 했어요.
The landlord said he's raising the deposit.
보증금 = key-money deposit, 집주인 = landlord
mistakes: Forgetting that present-tense verbs need -ㄴ다고/-는다고, not plain -다고: 간다고 했어요, not 가다고 했어요.

english: (someone) asked whether/if... — reporting a question someone asked
formNote: Attach -냐고 to verb and adjective stems alike in modern speech (가다 → 가냐고 했어요, 바쁘다 → 바쁘냐고 했어요). Past tense: -았/었냐고 했어요. The verb can be 묻다/물어보다 (asked) instead of 하다: 물어봤어요. In casual speech it contracts to -냬(요): 가냬 (= 가냐고 해). For nouns: N(이)냐고 했어요.
usage: Reporting a question with question word
He's asking if I have a boyfriend
She asked why I didn't come
examples: 엄마가 자꾸 취업 언제 하냐고 물어봐서 스트레스야.
My mom keeps asking when I'll get a job, it's stressful.
취업 = getting employed, classic parent question
소개팅남이 무슨 일 하냐고 했어요.
The blind-date guy asked what I do for work.
소개팅 = set-up date; very common social scene
사장님이 오늘 마감 칠 수 있냬요.
The boss is asking if I can close up today.
마감 치다 = close out the shift/work; -냬요 contraction
mistakes: Using -다고 (statement) when reporting a question — questions need -냐고: 오냐고 했어요, not 온다고 했어요.

english: it's worth doing / good enough to / can be done (reasonably)
formNote: Attach -ㄹ 만하다 to vowel-ending stems (보다 → 볼 만하다, 가다 → 갈 만하다) and -을 만하다 to consonant-ending stems (먹다 → 먹을 만하다, 참다 → 참을 만하다). It means something is worth the effort or is tolerable/decent. Past: -(으)ㄹ 만했어요. Note 만하다 is written as one word here (different from the 'as big as' 만하다).
examples: 그 드라마 생각보다 볼 만하던데? 한번 봐.
That drama's better than expected, honestly — give it a watch.
-던데 adds 'I found that...'; casual rec
회사 멀긴 한데 그래도 다닐 만해요.
The company's far, but it's still manageable to commute to.
다니다 = commute/attend; work-life realism
여기 가성비 좋아서 자주 올 만해요.
The value here is great, so it's worth coming often.
가성비 = cost-effectiveness, huge buzzword for young adults
mistakes: Adding -는: 보는 만해요 is wrong. The form is the future modifier -(으)ㄹ + 만하다 → 볼 만해요.

english: (it) ended up / came to be that... — a change of state, often not fully by your own choice
formNote: Attach -게 되다 to any verb stem (알다 → 알게 되다, 살다 → 살게 되다) and report the result in the past: -게 됐어요 (a contraction of -게 되었어요). It frames the outcome as something that came about through circumstances rather than pure personal will, so it sounds humble and natural. Present/future: -게 돼요 / -게 될 거예요.
usage: I ended up living in Korea
I came to find out that fact
I ended up quitting the company
examples: 일 때문에 서울에서 살게 됐어요.
Because of work, I ended up living in Seoul.
Polite self-intro for a newcomer
우연히 같은 동호회 하다가 사귀게 됐어요.
We happened to be in the same club and ended up dating.
동호회 = hobby club; common way couples meet
계약이 끝나서 이사 가게 됐어요.
My lease ended so it turns out I'm moving.
계약 = (housing) contract; relatable rent situation
mistakes: Translating it as plain 'became' and dropping 되다: 살았어요 means 'I lived', but 살게 됐어요 means 'I ended up living'.

english: while you're at it / since you're already doing it anyway
formNote: Attach -ㄴ 김에 to vowel-ending stems (나오다 → 나온 김에) and -은 김에 to consonant-ending stems (씻다 → 씻은 김에). You can also say 말이 나온 김에 (since it came up) and use the present -는 김에 for an ongoing action. It connects two clauses: 'since I already did X (anyway), I'll also do Y.' The Y clause carries the real point.
usage: Set phrase to add an errand
since you came, let's at least eat
examples: 편의점 가는 김에 내 커피도 하나 사다 줘.
Since you're going to the convenience store, grab me a coffee too.
편의점 = convenience store; casual favor
서울 올라온 김에 친구들도 만나고 가려고요.
Since I came up to Seoul, I'm planning to meet friends before I head back.
올라오다 = come up (to the capital)
말 나온 김에 우리 회식 날짜 정해요.
Since it came up, let's set the date for the team dinner.
Natural meeting-room phrase
mistakes: Using -을 김에 for a future plan — 김에 attaches to the past modifier -(으)ㄴ for completed actions (나온 김에), not -(으)ㄹ.

english: to the extent/point that... / so much that...
formNote: Attach -ㄹ 정도로 to vowel-ending stems (아프다 → 아플 정도로) and -을 정도로 to consonant-ending stems (죽다 → 죽을 정도로). It expresses the degree of something by giving a vivid 'enough to...' benchmark. You can end a clause with -(으)ㄹ 정도예요 (= to that extent). The clause after 정도로 states what the intensity leads to.
usage: I'm dead tired (tired to the point of dying)
I laughed so hard I teared up
to the point of being speechless
I ate till I was about to burst
examples: 어제 클럽에서 목 쉴 정도로 소리 질렀어요.
I screamed so much at the club last night that my voice went hoarse.
목 쉬다 = lose one's voice; nightlife scene
방값이 미쳤다 싶을 정도로 비싸요.
The rent is expensive to the point you'd think it's insane.
방값 = room/rent price; 미쳤다 = crazy, slangy
발표 전에 손이 떨릴 정도로 긴장했어요.
Before the presentation I was so nervous my hands were shaking.
발표 = presentation; work/uni context
mistakes: Saying -는 정도로 — the form is the future/potential modifier -(으)ㄹ + 정도로 (아플 정도로), not -는 정도로.
